profile.summary: LucaVirus is a language model for viruses that reads both nucleotide sequences (DNA or RNA) and protein sequences in one model. It was trained on OpenVirus, a corpus of 15.7 million viral sequences, and outputs per-token and per-sequence embeddings. These embeddings are used, or the model is fine-tuned, for tasks such as viral sequence classification, protein fitness prediction and antibody-antigen binding prediction.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: LucaVirus is an encoder-only Transformer with about 1 billion parameters. It was initialised from the weights of LucaOne, a general biological foundation model, then reduced to 12 transformer layers with a context window of 3072 tokens. The default checkpoint's config gives hidden size 2560, 20 attention heads and one vocabulary for nucleotides and amino acids. Pretraining combines masked language modelling with seven supervised tasks. Three are sequence-level (order taxonomy for nucleotide and protein sequences, and UniProt functional keywords for proteins) and four are token-level (gene prediction on nucleotides, and homologous superfamily, conserved domain and active site annotation on proteins). The user tells the tokenizer whether an input is a gene (DNA or RNA) or a protein. In the paper, downstream tasks train a small head (attention pooling, a fully connected layer and a prediction head) on frozen LucaVirus embeddings.

quotes.text: LucaVirus employs a customized encoder-only Transformer architecture with 1 billion parameters.
we reduced the model to 12 transformer layers while expanding the context window to 3072 tokens.
These downstream models share a unified, minimal architecture comprising a single attention-based pooling layer, a fully connected layer, and a task-specific prediction head
The model initializes its corresponding layers with weights derived from LucaOne’s latest training checkpoint at step 1,760,000.
The pre-training process integrates self-supervised masked language modeling (MLM) with seven biologically relevant supervised tasks
(i) Order taxonomy prediction for nucleotide sequences;
(iii) UniProt functional keyword prediction for protein sequences.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Five LucaVirus checkpoints are listed on Hugging Face under LucaGroup: default-step3.8M, prot-step3.8M, gene-step3.8M, mask-step1.4M and mask-step3.8M. The repository's training scripts describe the variants: one trained only with the masked language modelling task, one only on viral gene (DNA and RNA) data and one only on viral protein data. The repository's own embedding script downloads checkpoints from the authors' FTP server, while the Hugging Face checkpoints are loaded through the lucavirus package (version 1.1.1). A result should name the checkpoint and its revision; this page read the default checkpoint at revision 207da019. The README gives two figures for the LucaOne starting checkpoint: step 1,760,000 in its pretraining section and step=17600000 or 36000000 in its training scripts section. The paper says the pretrained weights, downstream models and training data are also on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.15703216).

facts.value: OpenVirus: 15.7 million viral sequences, 25.4 billion tokens, of which 23.7 billion nucleotide tokens from 10.4 million sequences (NCBI Virus and seven viral diversity studies) and 1.6 billion amino acid tokens from 5.2 million proteins (UniProtKB and MGnify). Nucleotide sequences were primarily sourced from the NCBI Virus database and seven independent viral diversity studies
Protein sequences were obtained from the UniProtKB and MGnify databases.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 3072 tokens, the context window stated in the paper. The config sets max_position_embeddings to 4096 with no_position_embeddings true. The repository examples truncate at 10240 tokens for nucleotides and 4096 for proteins, and can embed longer sequences in overlapping segments. The authors say an A100 handles about 2800 tokens at one time.

strengths.text: One model takes both nucleotide and protein sequences, and the authors model the two jointly.

quotes.text: **Unified Architecture**: Single model architecture handling multiple biological modalities.
By jointly modeling nucleotide and amino acid sequences, LucaVirus captures the unique grammatical and semantic dependencies underlying viral evolution

strengths.text: The training corpus is viral only and covers all known viral taxa and hosts from all three domains of life, and it has been released on Hugging Face.

quotes.text: The OpenVirus data set covers all known viral taxa.
The data set includes viruses infecting all three domains and six kingdoms of cellular life
OpenVirus Datasets are now available on HuggingFace.

strengths.text: The Hugging Face checkpoints work with the standard transformers Auto classes and include heads for sequence and token classification, so fine-tuning needs little custom code.

quotes.text: **Hugging Face Native**: Full support for `AutoModel`, `AutoModelForMaskedLM`, `AutoModelForSequenceClassification`, `AutoModelForTokenClassification`, `AutoConfig`, and `AutoTokenizer`.

limitations.text: At about 950 million parameters it is a large model. The authors recommend large-memory GPUs (A100, H100, H200) and fall back to CPU, which is slower, when a sequence does not fit.

run_guide.summary: Install the lucavirus package and compute an embedding for one nucleotide sequence with the default Hugging Face checkpoint.
prerequisites: Python with pip. The model card pins lucavirus==1.1.1, tokenizers==0.19.1 and transformers==4.41.2.
The card's code uses a CUDA GPU if available and the CPU otherwise. The authors recommend large-memory GPUs such as A100, H100 or H200 for long sequences.
Weights are under MIT according to the model card and are not gated. The code repository is Apache-2.0.

steps.title: Install the package
steps.shell:
pip install lucavirus==1.1.1
pip install tokenizers==0.19.1
pip install transformers==4.41.2
steps.explanation: Installs the lucavirus package and the pinned tokenizers and transformers versions given in the model card.

steps.title: Embed a nucleotide sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
import lucavirus
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

model_id = "LucaGroup/LucaVirus-default-step3.8M"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    model_id,
    trust_remote_code=True,
    force_download=True
)

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    model_id,
    task_level="token_level",
    task_type="embedding",
    trust_remote_code=True,
    force_download=True
)

device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model.to(device)
model.eval()

nucleotide_sequence = "ATGCGTACGTTAGC"
nucleotide_inputs = tokenizer(
    nucleotide_sequence,
    seq_type="gene",
    return_tensors="pt",
    add_special_tokens=True
)
new_nucleotide_inputs = {}
for item in nucleotide_inputs.items():
    new_nucleotide_inputs[item[0]] = item[1].to(device)
nucleotide_inputs = new_nucleotide_inputs

with torch.no_grad():
    nucleotide_outputs = model(**nucleotide_inputs)
    nucleotide_last_hidden = nucleotide_outputs.last_hidden_state
    mean_nucleotide_embedding = nucleotide_last_hidden[:, 1:-1, :].mean(dim=1)
print(f"Nucleotide Embedding Shape: {nucleotide_last_hidden.shape}")
print(mean_nucleotide_embedding)
PY
steps.explanation: The nucleotide part of the model card's feature extraction example, wrapped in a shell heredoc, with the protein part, the unused training imports and some print lines left out. For a protein, pass seq_type="prot" as the card does.

outputs: The shape of the per-token embedding matrix, [batch_size, seq_len + 2, hidden_size], and the mean-pooled embedding vector, printed to the terminal.
limitations: These commands were read from the model card and have not been executed by Rewire.

For long sequences and batch embedding from FASTA, the authors point to the repository script src/get_embedding.py, which needs the conda environment and requirements.txt from the README and downloads checkpoints from the authors' FTP server.
force_download=True in the card's code downloads the weights again on every run.

notes: The bioRxiv preprint returned error 1015 and was not read; the published paper (doi 10.1093/nsr/nwag376, CC BY 4.0) was read from Europe PMC. Licence mismatch: repository Apache-2.0, Hugging Face cards MIT. The README states two different LucaOne starting checkpoints (step 1,760,000 in section 3; step=17600000 or 36000000 in section 8); both are reported. The paper mentions structured access controls as a dual-use safeguard, but the Hugging Face weights are not gated. The LucaOne checkpoints under LucaGroup are a separate model.
